finding.title: OS Command Injection
finding.trigger: An attacker can inject a crafted string that, when converted to an integer, results in unexpected behavior or system calls.
finding.assumptions: The input is not sanitized before being converted to an integer. The system might allow special characters or control sequences that could be misinterpreted.

parsed.refutation_attempt: Checked for command execution or system calls around the use of atoi on file_contents. No such calls exist; atoi simply parses an integer. The source is a file read from a system-protected path, but even if manipulated, atoi would not invoke shell commands. No check neutralises the conversion, but the sink is not a command injection point.

finding.title: Buffer Overflow
finding.trigger: If the file content exceeds MAX_STR_LENGTH, it can overflow the buffer, leading to undefined behavior.
finding.assumptions: The file content is not checked for length before being read into the buffer.

parsed.refutation_attempt: Checked that fgets reads at most MAX_STR_LENGTH-1 characters and null-terminates, thus preventing buffer overflow. Verified that the source of data is a system file (trusted in this context) and the buffer size is constant. No path allows more than 19 characters to be written into file_contents.

finding.title: OS Command Injection
finding.trigger: An attacker can influence the brightness value, which might be used in a way that leads to unexpected system calls or behavior.
finding.assumptions: The brightness value is not sanitized or validated before being written to the file.

parsed.refutation_attempt: Checked that the source of the brightness value is derived from the current brightness read from a system file and subsequently bounded by the explicit checks at lines 67-71.  No path from an attacker‑controlled input to the fprintf call exists; fprintf is used only to write a numeric value to a file descriptor, not to invoke shell commands.  The value is converted to an integer and constrained before being written, so there is no opportunity for command injection.

finding.title: OS Command Injection
finding.trigger: The new brightness value, derived from user input, is written to a file without proper validation, which could lead to unexpected behavior or system calls.
finding.assumptions: The new brightness value is not sanitized or validated before being written to the file.

parsed.refutation_attempt: Checked for OS command execution calls (system, exec, popen, etc.). None present. The sink function write_brightness only opens the file for writing and uses fprintf to write an integer value, which cannot invoke shell commands. Additionally, new_brightness is clamped between MIN_BRIGHTNESS (3000) and MAX_BRIGHTNESS (120000), preventing any non‑numeric or excessively large values. The untrusted data path is fully sanitized before the sink, and no command‑invocation APIs are used. Therefore, OS Command Injection does not exist.
